glosses.notes: Used when schedules, interests, ideas, or positions do not match and create friction.

examples.sentence: 这两个会议原来分开安排得好好的，可是客户临时改时间以后，下午的行程一下子就冲突了，谁也走不开。
她本来想周末陪父母去医院检查，可是公司正好通知她必须去外地见客户，两个安排明显冲突，她只能先打电话解释。
大家都喜欢安静简单的风格，但是对方说颜色越亮越好看，所以双方的意见一直冲突，这个方案改了很多次还是没有结果。

example_translations.translation: The two meetings had originally been arranged separately without any issue, but after the client changed the time at the last minute, the afternoon schedule suddenly clashed and nobody could step away.

She had planned to accompany her parents to the hospital for a checkup that weekend, but the company happened to notify her that she had to travel to meet a client, so the two plans clearly conflicted and she could only call to explain first.
Everyone liked a quiet and simple style, but the other side said brighter colors looked better, so the two sides kept being at odds and the plan still had no result after many revisions.

glosses.notes: Often means looking up to someone with strong respect or even devotion, not just ordinary liking.

examples.sentence: 弟弟从小就崇拜那个总在雨天帮老人过马路的警察，所以每次路过派出所，都会停下来多看两眼。
她年轻时很崇拜那位写歌的人，家里到现在还留着那张旧海报，边上全是她当年写下的感想。
新来的学生不是一开始就崇拜老师，而是看见老师每天准备上课到很晚、回答问题又很认真，所以后来越来越崇拜他。

example_translations.translation: My younger brother has admired that police officer deeply since childhood because he always helps elderly people cross the road on rainy days, so every time we pass the station, he stops to look a little longer.
When she was young, she adored that songwriter so much that the old poster is still hanging in her home, with the edges filled with thoughts she wrote down back then.

The new student did not admire the teacher from the very beginning. Only after seeing the teacher stay late preparing class every day and answer questions very seriously did he come to admire him more and more.

glosses.notes: Can be used for rebuilding physical places and for rebuilding trust, order, or confidence after damage.

examples.sentence: 洪水退了以后，村里先把倒下的桥和路一点一点重建起来，好让孩子开学之前能安全走到学校。
那次合作闹得很不愉快，后来经理没有急着要求大家马上忘掉，而是花了好几个月一点一点重建彼此的信任。
老街着火以后，大家原来以为生意很难再做下去，没想到几年后政府和大家一起把那一带慢慢重建成了新的夜市。

example_translations.translation: After the floodwaters receded, the village first rebuilt the collapsed bridge and road little by little so the children could walk to school safely before the term began.
That round of cooperation ended badly, and afterward the manager did not rush everyone to forget it. Instead, she spent several months gradually rebuilding mutual trust.

After the old street caught fire, people originally thought business there would be hard to continue, but a few years later the government and local people slowly rebuilt the area into a new night market together.

glosses.notes: A colloquial preposition meaning toward or directed at someone, as in 冲我笑 or 冲孩子发火.

examples.sentence: 店门刚打开，老板就冲排在最前面的老人笑了笑，还先把一把干净的椅子搬到门口，请他慢慢坐下等。
你别一着急就冲孩子发火，他只是还没有把情况说清楚，先让他把书包放下，再慢慢问也不迟。
这话不是冲你说的，我只是看见大家最近太累，才想提醒一下别把每件小事都放在心里。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the shop door opened, the owner smiled toward the elderly man at the very front of the line, then even moved a clean chair to the entrance and invited him to sit and wait slowly.
Do not direct your anger at the child the moment you get anxious. He just has not explained the situation clearly yet, so let him set down his schoolbag first and ask slowly afterward.
Those words were not directed at you. I only saw that everyone has been too tired lately, so I wanted to remind people not to take every little thing to heart.

glosses.notes: Used for drawing prizes or taking part in a lucky draw activity.

examples.sentence: 商场周年活动那天，很多人一大早就排队进门，买完指定商品以后还拿着收据去服务台抽奖，希望能把洗衣机带回家。
公司年会快结束的时候，主持人把最后几张纸拿在手里准备抽奖，台下的人一边鼓掌一边低头看自己前面拿到的号。
这家书店为了让孩子暑假多看书，规定借满五本就能参加一次抽奖，所以门口总有人拿着卡等结果。

example_translations.translation: On the day of the shopping mall anniversary event, many people lined up at the entrance early in the morning. After buying the required items, they even took their receipts to the service desk for the prize draw, hoping to bring home a washing machine.

As the company annual party was nearing its end, the host held the last few slips of paper in hand to start the lucky draw, while people below the stage applauded and lowered their heads to look at the number they had received earlier.

To encourage children to read more during summer vacation, this bookstore set a rule that borrowing five books earned one chance in the raffle, so there were always people standing by the door with their cards waiting for the result.

glosses.notes: Describes ideas or explanations that are hard to picture directly because they are not concrete.

examples.sentence: 老师刚讲到那个抽象的概念时，后排几个学生都听得有点乱，直到她拿生活里的例子慢慢解释，大家才跟上。
这幅画颜色并不多，可是线条太抽象，爷爷站在前面看了半天，还是没看出画的是海边还是山路。
经理写的说明太抽象，新来的同事看完以后还是不知道先做哪一步，只好又回去把流程一条一条问清楚。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher first reached that abstract concept, several students in the back grew a little lost. Only after she slowly explained it with examples from everyday life did everyone catch up.
This painting did not use many colors, but the lines were too abstract. Grandfather stood there looking for a long time and still could not tell whether it showed the seaside or a mountain road.
The explanation the manager wrote was too abstract, so the new coworker still did not know which step to do first after reading it and had to go back and ask through the process item by item.

glosses.notes: A vivid everyday verb for feeling troubled or weighed down by a problem.

examples.sentence: 房租和药费一下子都赶到这个月来，母亲坐在那里越算越愁，连已经热好的面也一直没有吃。
孩子半夜还没有回家，父亲站在阳台上一次一次看楼下，越等越愁，手机拿起来又放下，不知道先给谁打。
眼看演出只剩两天，但是借来的灯还没有送到，负责布置的人全都愁得睡不着，第二天一早又去仓库问消息。

example_translations.translation: The rent and medical costs both landed in the same month, and Mother sat there growing more worried the longer she did the numbers. Even the noodles that had already been heated stayed uneaten.

The child still had not come home by midnight, and Father kept standing on the balcony looking downstairs again and again. The longer he waited, the more he fretted, picking up his phone and putting it down without knowing whom to call first.

With only two days left before the performance and the borrowed lights still not delivered, the people in charge of the setup were so worried they could not sleep and went back to ask the warehouse for news early the next morning.

glosses.notes: Used for organizing people, money, materials, and plans before an event or project.

examples.sentence: 为了筹备社区的旧书交换日，大家忙了一个星期，从借桌子到写通知都分好了人，下雨的时候去哪里也提前想到了。
他们筹备婚礼的时候并没有一味追求热闹，而是先把双方老人坐得舒服不舒服想清楚，再决定桌子怎么摆。
新店开门前的最后半个月最累，老板白天跑手续，晚上还要和大家一起筹备菜单、灯光和试营业的安排。

example_translations.translation: To prepare for the community used-book exchange day, everyone stayed busy for a week, assigning people to everything from borrowing tables to writing notices, and they even decided ahead of time where to go if it rained.

When they were preparing the wedding, they did not blindly chase excitement. Instead, they first thought carefully about whether the elderly people on both sides would sit comfortably before deciding how to arrange the tables.

The last half month before the new shop opened was the most exhausting. The owner ran around handling procedures during the day and still had to work with everyone at night arranging the menu, lighting, and trial-opening plans.

glosses.notes: Describes something worked out or understood at an early stage, before the full result is confirmed.

examples.sentence: 医生看完检查以后先给了一个初步判断，说大问题暂时看不出来，但是还得再观察两天，大家这才稍微放下心。
会议开了一个上午，大家终于拿出了初步方案，很多细节以后还要改，但是下周先做哪一步已经很清楚了。
大家根据门口的录像做了初步分析，发现那个人不是路过才进去的，而是前几天已经来过这里好几次。

example_translations.translation: After reviewing the examination, the doctor first gave a preliminary judgment, saying that no major problem could be seen for the moment, but two more days of observation were still needed. Only then did everyone relax a little.
After meeting all morning, everyone finally produced an initial plan. Many details still needed to be revised later, but it was already clear which step should be done first next week.

Based on the video from the entrance, everyone made an initial analysis and found that the person had not gone in by chance while passing by, but had already come here several times in the previous days.

glosses.notes: Used when a person or team enters the scene, stage, or competition.

examples.sentence: 节目快开始的时候，主持人刚报完名字，那个一直在后台深呼吸的年轻演员就整理好衣服，然后出场了。
下半场刚开了几分钟，教练就让一直坐在边上的老队员出场，希望他先让场上的人安静下来，别再让大家乱起来。
学校排练那个戏的时候，最小的那个孩子每次一出场都先忘了自己该站哪里，老师只好在下面轻轻抬手提醒。

example_translations.translation: Just as the program was about to begin and the host had finished announcing his name, the young actor who had been taking deep breaths backstage straightened his clothes and then came on stage.
Only a few minutes into the second half, the coach sent the veteran player on, hoping he could calm the people on the field first and keep everyone from getting chaotic again.
When the school rehearsed that play, the youngest child forgot where to stand every time he came on, so the teacher had no choice but to lift a hand gently from below to remind him.

glosses.notes: A formal adjective used in set phrases such as 初等教育 or 初等数学 for elementary-level study.

examples.sentence: 新来的老师教初等数学很有耐心，学生有一步没想明白的时候，她总会先把最基本的图画出来，再让大家自己说。
她毕业以后先去了山里的小学做初等教育，白天上课，晚上还去找那些总请假的孩子，劝他们回来读书。
这本资料看起来很厚，其实前半部分讲的都是初等物理的基本概念，所以老师才放心拿它给刚进实验室的人先打底。

example_translations.translation: The new teacher is very patient when teaching elementary mathematics. Whenever a student does not understand one step, she first draws the most basic diagram and then lets everyone explain it in their own words.

After graduating, she first went to a mountain primary school to do elementary education, teaching during the day and then going out at night to find the children who were always absent and persuade them to come back to study.

This reference book looks very thick, but the first half is really all basic concepts from elementary physics, which is why the teacher felt comfortable using it to give newcomers to the lab a foundation.

glosses.notes: Used for crossing the border and leaving one country for another.

examples.sentence: 父亲第一次自己带孩子出境，前一晚把护照、机票和酒店地址检查了三遍，生怕到了机场才发现少带了一样。
海关通知这批货暂时不能出境以后，负责人马上回办公室改计划，又联系仓库把已经装好的东西重新记了一遍。
她原来打算暑假带母亲出境看看海，可是一算路上转车太累，就改成先去近一点的地方试试。

example_translations.translation: It was the first time Father was taking the child out of the country by himself, so the night before he checked the passport, ticket, and hotel address three times, afraid that he would only discover something missing after reaching the airport.

After customs notified them that this batch of goods could not leave the country for the time being, the person in charge immediately returned to the office to revise the plan and contacted the warehouse to record the packed goods again.
She had originally planned to take her mother abroad during summer vacation to see the sea, but after calculating how tiring the transfers would be, she changed it to trying somewhere closer first.

glosses.notes: Means putting in real effort or muscle to help get something done.

examples.sentence: 楼下那位老人搬家时，大家都没有只站着看，年轻人帮着抬东西，年纪大一点的人也在边上出力，把小东西一点一点收好。
这次活动能办成，不只是经理一个人安排得好，而是每个部门都肯出力，连平时最少说话的人也主动留下来加班。
他嘴上总说自己帮不上什么大忙，可是真到了最乱的时候，还是他先卷起袖子出力，把车上的东西一个一个搬进去。

example_translations.translation: When the elderly man downstairs was moving house, nobody just stood there watching. The younger people helped carry things, and the older ones also lent a hand from the side, putting the smaller items away one by one.

This event was successful not simply because the manager arranged things well, but because every department was willing to contribute effort, and even the person who usually spoke the least volunteered to stay and work overtime.

He always says he cannot help with anything major, but when things were truly at their most chaotic, he was still the first to roll up his sleeves and help out, carrying the things off the vehicle one by one.

glosses.notes: A common spoken adjective for being widely known.

examples.sentence: 那家卖面的店在这一带很出名，不到十二点门口就排满了人，但是老板还是一碗一碗慢慢做，不肯少放一点东西。
她年轻时在学校里就很出名，不是因为成绩最好，而是因为谁有难事去找她，她总能把话说得特别让人安心。
这座小城原来一直很安静，但是后来因为秋天那条老街慢慢出名，每年一到天凉就有很多人专门来看。

example_translations.translation: That noodle place is famous around here. Before noon, the door is already full of people, but the owner still makes each bowl slowly and refuses to skimp on what goes into it.

She was already well-known at school when she was young, not because she had the best grades, but because whenever someone with a problem went to her, she always knew how to speak in a way that made people feel at ease.
This small city used to be very quiet, but later it gradually became famous because of that old street in autumn, and every year when the weather turns cool many people come specially to see it.

glosses.notes: Often appears in 有出入 when numbers, memories, or accounts do not match exactly.

examples.sentence: 会计把两份报表对到半夜，才发现数字里确实有出入，于是第二天一早又去仓库把原来的记录重新看了一遍。
两个人回忆那天的经过时细节有些出入，一个记得是下午下雨以后发生的，另一个却坚持说天还亮着。
医生看完片子以后说估计结果不会差太多，但是要不要下结论，还得等检查结果出来看看有没有出入。

example_translations.translation: The accountant compared the two reports until midnight before discovering there really was a discrepancy in the numbers, so early the next morning he went back to the warehouse and looked through the original records again.

When the two people recalled what had happened that day, there were some differences in the details. One remembered that it happened after the afternoon rain, while the other insisted it was still light outside.
After looking at the images, the doctor said the result probably would not differ too much, but to make a real judgment they still had to wait for the test results and see whether there was any gap.

glosses.notes: Used when formally showing a document, pass, ticket, or certificate for inspection.

examples.sentence: 进站的时候工作人员请大家提前出示身份证和车票，别等走到门前才低头找，那样后面的人都会停下来。
保安看到陌生车辆开进院子，先上前请司机出示通行证，又问他是来送货还是来接人，确认以后才放行。
她去银行补办卡的时候，工作人员先让她出示旧卡和几份证明材料，还当场对了一下手机里收到的短信。

example_translations.translation: When entering the station, the staff asked everyone to present their ID cards and tickets in advance instead of waiting until reaching the entrance to search for them, because that would make the people behind stop too.

When the security guard saw an unfamiliar vehicle drive into the yard, he first stepped forward and asked the driver to show a pass, then asked whether he was there to deliver goods or pick someone up, and only let him through after confirming.
When she went to the bank to replace her card, the staff first asked her to present the old card and several supporting documents, then checked the text message on her phone on the spot.

glosses.notes: Often refers to going out for travel or a day trip for pleasure.

examples.sentence: 连着下了几天雨以后，太阳一出来，院子里的老人就商量周末一起出游，想趁天气好去河边走走，顺便在外面吃顿饭。
公司原来计划这个月末集体出游，但是后来有人家里突然有事，经理就把行程改短，免得大家来回太赶。
父母难得一起休息，孩子一听说全家要出游，从前一晚就把零食和相机装进包里，早上天一亮就催着出门。

example_translations.translation: After several days of rain in a row, the moment the sun came out, the elderly people in the courtyard began discussing a weekend outing together, hoping to take advantage of the good weather to walk by the river and have a meal outside.

The company had originally planned a group trip for the end of the month, but later someone suddenly had a family matter, so the manager shortened the itinerary to keep everyone from rushing too much on the way there and back.

It was rare for both parents to have time off together, so the moment the child heard the whole family was going on an outing, he packed snacks and a camera into his bag the night before and began urging everyone to leave as soon as it was light.

glosses.notes: Introduces a reason or motive, especially in patterns like 出于关心 or 出于礼貌.

examples.sentence: 他当时那么做并不是想抢着表现，只是出于关心，怕这件事再拖下去会让大家更累，所以才先去处理最急的部分。
奶奶一直把要用的东西放在门口，不是因为舍不得花钱，而是出于习惯，总觉得下雨天出门前先拿上才安心。
她出于礼貌没有当场指出对方说错了哪一句，只是在会后把资料重新整理好，再发过去让大家自己看清楚。

example_translations.translation: He did not act that way because he wanted to show off. It was out of concern, because he was afraid that if this matter kept dragging on everyone would become even more tired, so he handled the most urgent part first.
Grandma always keeps the things she needs by the door not because she hates spending money, but because of habit. She feels at ease only if she picks them up before going out on a rainy day.

Out of politeness, she did not point out on the spot which sentence the other person had said incorrectly. She only reorganized the materials after the meeting and sent them again so everyone could see clearly for themselves.

glosses.notes: A formal word used in 除了 for except, 除以 for divide by, and some verb uses meaning remove.

examples.sentence: 后院的草一个月没管，父亲周末一早就拿着工具把院子里的杂草一片一片除了，忙到中午后背都湿透了。
老师怕大家没有想清楚，就先把题写在黑板上，让我们一步一步算清楚六十除以四以后每个人到底能分到多少。
除了值夜班的人以外，办公室里的人吃完晚饭都下楼去帮忙搬东西，连平时最少说话的人也主动伸手。

example_translations.translation: The backyard had been left alone for a month, so early on the weekend morning Father took his tools and removed the weeds from the yard patch by patch, working until his whole back was soaked by noon.

The teacher was afraid everyone had not really thought it through, so she first wrote the problem on the blackboard and had us work out step by step how much each person would get after dividing sixty by four.
Except for the people on the night shift, everyone in the office went downstairs after dinner to help carry things, and even the person who usually spoke the least reached out to help on their own.

glosses.notes: Introduces the one condition under which something different would happen.

examples.sentence: 除非医生明天亲口说可以出院，不然父亲怎么劝都不肯把包收好，他总觉得再多看一晚才放心。
这件事除非大家把旧记录和新方案放在一起慢慢对，不然光靠记忆争半天，最后还是谁都说服不了谁。
孩子答应得再快也没有用，除非他今天晚上真的把作业写完、书包整理好，母亲才会让他明天一早跟同学去打球。

example_translations.translation: Unless the doctor personally says tomorrow that he can be discharged, Father refuses to pack his bag no matter how much people urge him, because he feels he can relax only after one more night of observation.
Unless everyone puts the old records and the new plan together and checks them slowly, arguing for half a day from memory alone will still end with nobody convincing anyone else.

It does not matter how quickly the child promises. Unless he really finishes his homework and organizes his schoolbag tonight, Mother will not let him go play ball with his classmates tomorrow morning.

glosses.notes: Used for storing physical goods, data, power, or supplies for later use.

examples.sentence: 奶奶每年冬天都会在阳台上储存一些晒干的菜，说天气最冷的时候不想天天往市场跑，家里先放着这些就安心。
厨房后面专门空出一个小房间储存米、面和油，就是怕节日前来买东西的人太多，前面柜子里的货一下子不够卖。
山上的那座旧水塔原来就是给周围的人储存雨水用的，所以修好以后，大家一下雨还是会先去看看水位。

example_translations.translation: Every winter Grandma stores some dried vegetables on the balcony, saying that when the weather is coldest she does not want to run to the market every day and feels more at ease with these things already set aside at home.

A small room behind the kitchen is kept empty especially to store rice, flour, and oil, because they worry too many customers will come before holidays and the goods in the front cabinets will suddenly not be enough to sell.

That old water tower on the mountain was originally used to store rainwater for the people living around it, so even after it was repaired, everyone still goes to check the water level first whenever it rains.

glosses.notes: Used for giving an official punishment after someone breaks a rule.

examples.sentence: 公司明明已经写清楚安全规定，但是他还是为了省事跳过了关键步骤，结果不仅自己受伤，还让全组一起接受处罚。
老师没有急着处罚那个打碎窗户的学生，而是先把前后经过问清楚，确定不是故意以后，才决定让他留下来帮忙收拾。
司机连续几次闯红灯以后，交警当场说明这次处罚不会只记一次分，还要让他回去重新参加安全学习。

example_translations.translation: The company had clearly written out the safety rules, but he still skipped a key step just to save trouble. As a result, not only was he injured himself, he also caused the whole team to receive punishment.

The teacher did not rush to punish the student who broke the window. Instead, she first asked through the whole sequence of events, and only after confirming it was not intentional did she decide to have him stay and help clean up.

After the driver ran red lights several times, the traffic police explained on the spot that this penalty would not simply mean losing one set of points and that he would also have to go back and attend safety training again.

glosses.notes: Can mean the act of saving money and the money saved.

examples.sentence: 父母这些年一直省着花，不是舍不得享受，而是想多做一点储蓄，好让孩子以后读书或者看病时不用太发愁。
她工作后的第一件事就是去银行开了个账户，把每个月剩下的钱固定存进去，当作自己的小储蓄。
老人退休以后没有乱花那笔补偿，而是把大部分都变成储蓄，准备以后房子要修或者身体不舒服时再用。

example_translations.translation: For all these years, the parents have spent carefully not because they are unwilling to enjoy life, but because they want to build up more savings so that later the child will not have to worry too much about school or medical treatment.
The first thing she did after starting work was go to the bank to open an account and deposit the leftover money from each month on a fixed basis as her own little savings fund.
After retiring, the old man did not spend that compensation carelessly. Instead, he turned most of it into savings, planning to use it later if the house needed repairs or his health failed.

glosses.notes: An adverb showing something appears in many places or many parts of life.

examples.sentence: 这座小城不大，但是春天一到，河边、院里、墙角处处都是花，连上班最忙的人路过时也会忍不住放慢脚步。
他刚到新公司那几天总觉得不自在，因为处处都要重新适应，连一杯水放在哪里、文件该交给谁，都得先开口问。
母亲做事一向细心，孩子出门前她总要处处替他想到，从备用钥匙到水杯都先悄悄放进包里。

example_translations.translation: This small city is not large, but once spring arrives there are flowers everywhere by the river, in the courtyards, and at the corners of walls. Even the busiest workers cannot help slowing their steps when they pass.
During his first few days at the new company, he kept feeling uncomfortable because at every turn he had to readapt. He even had to ask where to put a cup of water and whom to hand documents to.
Mother is always careful in what she does, so before the child leaves home she thinks of everything for him, quietly placing everything from a spare key to a water cup into the bag ahead of time.

glosses.notes: Used for moving from one side of something to the other by going through it.

examples.sentence: 车刚开出城，太阳就从云里露出来，一道长长的光正好穿过前面的树和窗子，落在孩子手里的地图上。
他下班后没有走大路，而是穿过那条卖菜的小路回家，顺手买了豆腐和青菜，等到进门时汤也差不多该开了。
演员上台前先深吸了一口气，然后穿过后台那条窄窄的走道往灯光里走去，台下刚好也安静了下来。

example_translations.translation: Just after the car left the city, the sun came out from behind the clouds, and a long beam of light passed through the trees and the window ahead, landing on the map in the childs hands.

After work, he did not take the main road but instead went through the little road where vegetables were sold, bought tofu and greens on the way, and by the time he got home the soup was almost boiling.
Before going on stage, the actor took a deep breath, then passed through the narrow backstage corridor into the lights just as the audience below also became quiet.
